title: Approximating the Gomory mixed-integer cut closure using historical data
contribution: Proves that one finite set of aggregation multipliers gives the GMIC (and split) closure for every MILP in a family with fixed A and RHS on a rational lattice, and uses this to motivate a heuristic that reuses multipliers learned from historical instances, giving up to 1.49x work-unit speedups over default Gurobi on perturbed MIPLIB 2017 families.
problem_entry: Recurring operational MILPs (unit commitment) share A and vary b and c. The GMIC closure is strong but too costly to separate, and small RHS perturbations can change it completely (pp. 1-5).
key_idea: Learn aggregation multipliers lambda rather than cuts. Theorem 1 says a finite Lambda yields the GMIC closure for all RHS in b+Gamma (p. 6). Reuse lambdas stored as basis plus tableau row, chosen from k nearest, farthest or random training variations (pp. 6-10).
assumptions: Integral A and b. RHS on a lattice generated by rational vectors; all RHS only for pure IP (Cor. 1, p. 6). The experiments use multiplicative RHS +-10% and objective +-25% perturbations, outside the lattice model (p. 8).
proof_devices: legitimate (lambda,v) split-cut parametrisation with GMIC as the optimal v for fixed lambda (pp. 16-17)
Lemma 1: an undominated cut has basis support (p. 17)
RHS-independent sign cone C_sign(u) with decomposition u=u1+u2, u2 integral and divisible by M(Gamma), so u1 dominates (pp. 17-18)
Caratheodory plus integral extreme rays bound ||u1||_inf <= (m+n)M(Gamma)Delta, so the set of split directions is finite (p. 18)
pure-IP corollary via lambda=e_i on a fractional RHS row (p. 21)
experiments: Gurobi 11.0.2 at defaults, single thread, 3 seeds, given the optimal solution. 186 MIPLIB 2017 families (50 train / 5 test). Expert ceiling with and without collection time (exp+col 0.46x). On 50 expert-positive instances all learning variants beat the baseline in work units (best 1.49x; 1.40x on 14 hard instances); in total time only 1-closest wins on all 50, and all variants win on hard instances by 1.08-1.17x (pp. 7-12).
positioning: Short survey of ML for cut selection and generation and of sample-complexity theory (p. 2). Claims to be the first data-driven cut generation that significantly speeds up default commercial MILP on large benchmarks (abstract, p. 3). Links Cor. 1 to Wolsey's b-hull result (p. 6).
writing: Two contributions in one paragraph (p. 3). Five numbered findings with lead theses (pp. 11-12). Proofs in an appendix, where Theorems 2 and 3 duplicate Theorem 1 word for word (pp. 17-20). Symbol slips (Gamma for Lambda, pp. 6, 21).
limits_future: Overhead from recomputing the standard form and tableaux without solver internals (p. 12). Only modest perturbations (p. 13). Open: all RHS for MILP, group cuts, a better expert using infeasible bases (pp. 12-13).

method_links.note: Expert ceiling evaluated first; charging collection time makes most positive instances negative, which motivates learning; exp+col row (also Heuristic 6).
No stripped instrument: evaluation inside full default Gurobi; only the primal side is neutralised by supplying the optimal solution.
Theorem first, rule second ('Theorem 1 suggests a simple learning heuristic'); licenses a new practice instead of explaining an existing solver habit.
Boundary given only as an open all-RHS question and a stronger pure-IP corollary; no tightness example or counterexample to the lattice hypothesis.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: recurring-instance MILP with a structural license
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Fixed-A, varying-(b,c) operational setting; a finiteness theorem justifies reusing learned multipliers across instances; own related works on kNN transmission switching and similarity branching cited.

transferable: Learn aggregation weights lambda, not cuts; store them as (basis, tableau row) so the cut can be recomputed on new data (p. 10).
Report a ceiling that does not charge overhead, the same ceiling with overhead charged, and the learned method with all overhead, in both work units and wall time (pp. 9-12).
Isolate the dual side of a MILP experiment by giving the solver the optimal solution; fix threads and seeds (pp. 7-8).

Perturbation generator with rules by constraint type, preserving combinatorial rows and rejecting infeasible families; check the number of distinct optima and the difficulty after perturbing (pp. 8-9, 23).
Finiteness of a closure over a lattice of RHS: RHS-independent sign cone + integral/fractional split + Caratheodory (pp. 17-19).
coauthors: Berkay Becu, Feng Qiu, Alinson S. Xavier

quotes.text: Therefore, simple perturbation can change the GMIC closure dramatically.
However, when accounting for the time required to collect the cuts, most positive instances become negative, which motivates our learning approach.

title: Lagrangian dual with zero duality gap that admits decomposition
contribution: Constructs two reformulations of block-structured MIPs by primal-redundant, dual-separable constraints: a monomial (RLT-like) hierarchy and a vertex-based lifting. Their Lagrangian duals have zero duality gap and still decompose; the paper extends the monomial dual to general sparse MIPs via tree decompositions, gives multiplicative bounds for packing and covering, compares with scenario decomposition, and reports preliminary dual-bound gains.
problem_entry: Dualizing coupling constraints gives decomposable but gapped Lagrangian duals; the monolithic MIP has no gap but does not decompose. Can both be had at once? DP and augmented Lagrangian each miss one property (pp. 1-2).
key_idea: Add constraints F1(x1)+F2(x2)>=0 implied by x1=x2 binary that are separable after dualizing; affine F cannot help (Prop. 1). Monomial products for down-closed S give zero gap at S=2^[n] (Thm 2), vertex indicators give zero gap (Thm 5), and a tree decomposition of the intersection graph gives zero gap for general MIPs (Thm 8) (pp. 3-10).
assumptions: Binary coupling variables; down-closed S; relatively complete recourse for the packing bounds (enforceable by adding constraints); the V-Lagrangian only for star (two-stage) structure; nonnegative costs for Prop. 6 (pp. 2, 6, 8, 10).
proof_devices: primal (Geoffrion) characterisation of the Lagrangian dual over convex hulls of the blocks (p. 5, p. 17)
affine independence of all-subset-product vectors (Prop. 14, p. 19) with the simplex lemma, so hulls glue along shared coordinates (Prop. 13, p. 19)
induction removing a leaf of the tree decomposition (Lemma 2, pp. 20-21); projection of intersection within intersection of projections (p. 22)
fractional cover LP over good / k-good subsets for multiplicative packing/covering factors, adapted from Dey-Molinaro-Wang (pp. 6, 11, 22-29)
3-block cycle counterexample: all-monomial dual 0 vs OPT 1 (p. 9)
small worst-case instances n=2,k=1 against the bounds (p. 12, p. 30)
subgradient norm bound n+2 and explicit dual optima from SDA termination give iteration bounds; exponential lower-bound instance for SDA (pp. 32-37)
experiments: Preliminary: 10 blocks of stable set on random graphs, STAR-STAB and PATH-STAB, 10 instances each, 1200 s per method, warm start from 600 s of classical L, sequential subproblems, Gurobi 9.0.2 on a PC. Mean gaps: STAR Gurobi 10.0%, L 6.0%, QL 4.4%, VL 3.9%, SDA 8.6%; PATH Gurobi 10.8%, L 3.5%, QL 1.2%. No method terminates; averages only; graph size inconsistent between p. 12 and p. 37 (pp. 12-13, 37).
positioning: Strengthens Lemarechal-Renaud (Prop. 1); M-hierarchy 'similar to ... RLT ... but not the same', near Burer and their own sensitivity paper; V-Lagrangian compared with Ahmed's SDA by proofs both ways; cautions that more sophisticated two-stage methods exist and were not compared (pp. 2, 4-5, 8, 13).
writing: Five numbered contributions; theorems in the main text with proofs in an appendix (one wrong appendix cross-reference, p. 6 vs p. 18); the counterexample placed before the general theory; non-tightness admitted openly (Remark 2); the conclusion leads with the method's cost (pp. 2-13).
limits_future: Harder nonlinear subproblems, so the method suits many small blocks; V-Lagrangian limited to star structure; tightness of the hierarchy bounds open; naive implementation. Future: exact decomposable duals with easier subproblems, engineering, MIPLIB tree structures (pp. 8, 12-13).

method_links.note: Dual bounds are the deliverable; Lagrangian preferred to DP because bounds are available at any stop; primal-dual gaps reported.
Affine constraints proved useless; a cycle counterexample shows strong duality needs a tree; tightness left open with explicit small worst cases; exponential separation from SDA.
RLT/monomial lifting imported into Lagrangian decomposition; sparsity exploited through tree decomposition of the intersection graph.
Only small-case worst-instance search; no ceiling or stripped instrument; authors caution that stronger specialised two-stage methods were not compared (against Heuristic 2).

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Strengthen a decomposable dual by adding constraints redundant in the primal and separable after dualizing; first prove that affine ones cannot help.
Packing/covering multiplicative-bound technique from Dey-Molinaro-Wang sparse cuts reused for hierarchy levels of the M-Lagrangian.

transferable: Prove a reformulation class cannot help before searching inside it (Prop. 1, pp. 4, 17-18).
Use a 3-block cycle counterexample to motivate a tree-decomposition hypothesis (p. 9).
Solve a vertex-lifted dual in the original space: no-good cuts for x not in V plus enumeration of the few vertices with nonzero multiplier; cache y'(v) (Algorithm 1, pp. 7-8).
Compare with an existing exact method by a relative iteration bound and an exponential-separation instance (pp. 8, 33-37).
Exactness on trees via affine independence of the shared lifted coordinates plus induction on leaves (pp. 19-22).
Hierarchy-level approximation factors as values of fractional cover LPs over the subsets on which the level is exact (pp. 11, 25-29).

quotes.text: However, DP suffers from the disadvantage that we do not obtain any information on bounds until the algorithm terminates.
An open question is whether one can achieve Lagrangian duals with decomposability and zero duality gap while solving an "easier" subproblem in each iteration.
